audit_status.source_base: Greek Philemon text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Complete one-chapter draft reviewed for appeal rather than command, Onesimus as beloved sibling, partnership, debt language, anti-slavery dignity safeguards.

verses.restored: Paul, prisoner of Messiah Jesus, and Timothy the sibling, to Philemon our beloved and coworker,

familiar.text: Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer,

verses.restored: and to Apphia the sister, and to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the assembly in your house:

familiar.text: And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house:

verses.restored: Grace to you and peace from Divine our Father and Lord Jesus Messiah.

familiar.text: Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.restored: I give thanks to my Divine always, making remembrance of you in my prayers,

familiar.text: I thank my God, making mention of thee always in my prayers,

verses.restored: hearing of your love and the trust that you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the holy ones,

familiar.text: Hearing of thy love and faith, which thou hast toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all saints;

verses.restored: so that the partnership/fellowship of your trust may become effective in full knowledge of every good thing in us into Messiah.

familiar.text: That the communication of thy faith may become effectual by the acknowledging of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus.

verses.restored: For I had much joy and comfort because of your love, because the inward affections of the holy ones have been refreshed through you, sibling.

familiar.text: For we have great joy and consolation in thy love, because the bowels of the saints are refreshed by thee, brother.

verses.restored: Therefore, having much boldness in Messiah to command you what is fitting,

familiar.text: Wherefore, though I might be much bold in Christ to enjoin thee that which is convenient,

verses.restored: yet because of love I rather appeal, being such a one as Paul, an elder, and now also prisoner of Messiah Jesus.

familiar.text: Yet for love’s sake I rather beseech thee, being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.

verses.restored: I appeal to you concerning my child, whom I begot in chains, Onesimus,

familiar.text: I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds:

verses.restored: the one formerly useless to you but now useful both to you and to me,

familiar.text: Which in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable to thee and to me:

verses.restored: whom I sent back to you—him, that is, my own inward affections.

familiar.text: Whom I have sent again: thou therefore receive him, that is, mine own bowels:

verses.restored: I wished to keep him with myself, so that on your behalf he might serve me in the chains of the good news,

familiar.text: Whom I would have retained with me, that in thy stead he might have ministered unto me in the bonds of the gospel:

verses.restored: but apart from your consent I wanted to do nothing, so that your good might not be according to compulsion but according to willingness.

familiar.text: But without thy mind would I do nothing; that thy benefit should not be as it were of necessity, but willingly.

verses.restored: For perhaps because of this he was separated for an hour, so that you might have him back forever,

familiar.text: For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever;

verses.restored: no longer as enslaved, but beyond enslaved: a beloved sibling, especially to me, and how much more to you, both in flesh and in the Lord.

familiar.text: Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but how much more unto thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord?

verses.restored: Therefore, if you hold me as partner, receive him as me.

familiar.text: If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself.

verses.restored: And if he wronged you in anything or owes, charge this to me.

familiar.text: If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account;

verses.restored: I, Paul, write with my own hand: I will repay, not to say to you that you owe me even yourself.

familiar.text: I Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will repay it: albeit I do not say to thee how thou owest unto me even thine own self besides.

verses.restored: Yes, sibling, may I benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my inward affections in Messiah.

familiar.text: Yea, brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: refresh my bowels in the Lord.

verses.restored: Having been persuaded of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even beyond what I say.

familiar.text: Having confidence in thy obedience I wrote unto thee, knowing that thou wilt also do more than I say.

verses.restored: At the same time also prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be graciously given to you.

familiar.text: But withal prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you.

verses.restored: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Messiah Jesus, greets you,

familiar.text: There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus;

verses.restored: as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, my coworkers.

familiar.text: Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellowlabourers.

verses.restored: The grace of the Lord Jesus Messiah be with your spirit.

familiar.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

safety_note: Philemon must never be used to sanctify slavery. The text is an appeal that pressures Philemon toward receiving Onesimus no longer as enslaved but beyond enslaved, as beloved sibling. The source-audit trajectory should preserve Onesimus' dignity, agency, and siblinghood and flag the letter for deep reception-history audit.
translation_notes: Koinonos/koinonia language is rendered partner/partnership to foreground shared participation.
Paul appeals rather than commands, but the appeal is morally forceful.
Verse 16 is the hinge: no longer as enslaved, but beyond enslaved: beloved sibling.
